stem:
Bela compares birds and most mammals after fertilisation. She asks where the fertilised egg develops into an embryo in each case.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: In birds the fertilised egg is laid and develops during hatching; in most mammals the embryo develops inside the female body until birth.
In birds the embryo develops inside the female body until birth; in most mammals the fertilised egg is laid and develops during hatching.
The same comparison applies before fertilisation as after fertilisation.
Birds and most mammals develop in the same place because both start from a fertilised egg.

teacher.key_rationale: After fertilisation, birds lay the egg and development continues during hatching; most mammal embryos develop inside the female body with support until birth. Swapping places, ignoring the after-fertilisation condition, or treating both as the same place is wrong.
